show on the slide — they go to the PDF notes and the presenter view. Put the "how to

## Math Renders Crisply

Client-side KaTeX, vendored locally. Write `$...$` inline, or `$$...$$` for a block:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{J}_{\text{GRPO}}(\theta) &= \mathbb{E}\!\left[\,\tfrac{1}{G}\sum_{i=1}^{G}\tfrac{1}{|o_i|}\sum_{t}\min\big(r_{i,t}\,\hat{A}_{i,t},\;\operatorname{clip}(r_{i,t},1-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon)\,\hat{A}_{i,t}\big)\right.\\
&\qquad\left.-\;\beta\,\mathbb{D}_{\text{KL}}\big(\pi_\theta\,\|\,\pi_{\text{ref}}\big)\right]
\end{aligned}
$$

- The PDF driver waits for `document.fonts.ready`, so math never falls back to Times
- Notation like `\boldsymbol`, `\mathcal`, `\operatorname` all render

::: notes
This GRPO objective is the deck's built-in regression test for the PDF pipeline: if the
KaTeX webfonts ever lose the race to the print snapshot, this slide is where it shows.
:::

## Stacked Layout

![](assets/demo/placeholder.svg){.centerfig}

- Use a **figure on top, bullets below** when a figure is wide
- Tag a full-width image `{.bigfig}` to opt out of the inline height cap, or
  `{.centerfig}` (used here) to centre it with a sensible cap
- Good for wide diagrams and side-by-side panels

::: notes
Wide figures read better stacked (figure on top spanning the width, bullets beneath)
than squeezed into a column. Portrait figures read better in the two-column layout.
:::

## Bullets, Hand-off and Notes

- Regular bullets carry the body text
  - nested bullets read at the same size, slightly indented
- **Bold** highlights a keyword in the accent colour

::: transition
A transition line — accent, sits low on the slide, hands off to the next idea →
:::

::: notes
Two reusable blocks shown here: `::: transition` (the accent hand-off line) and these
speaker notes. A `::: caption` block (grey, auto-pinned to the slide foot) is also
available for figure sources — see docs/CONVENTIONS.md. Keep visible copy short; push
detail into the notes.
:::
